slot: TAKE FROM THE LEDGER — do not `ls`
not_this_lane: Pre-existing on the spine. Raised here because it is the one red in this lane's gate set and it reddens the leave test file for every lane that runs it.
defect: leave_api.assert_employee_directory_manager(UUID, UUID) is SECURITY DEFINER, owned by mnt_leave_definer, and 0183_leave_api_create_employee.sql issues no REVOKE for it — so it keeps PostgreSQL's default EXECUTE TO PUBLIC. Every sibling function in the same file is explicitly REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, mnt_rt before being granted.

evidence.grep: grep -rn assert_employee_directory_manager backend/crates/platform/db/migrations/*.sql → 3 lines: CREATE (0183:61), ALTER ... OWNER (0183:125), PERFORM (0183:141). No GRANT, no REVOKE.
evidence.failing_test: backend/crates/leave/adapter-postgres/tests/leave_rls_surfaces_as_runtime_role.rs::leave_command_preprovision_and_privilege_matrix_are_fail_closed — 'command role receives exactly six public entrypoints and no helpers'; observed eight (create_employee, assert_employee_directory_manager).

severity: low direct risk — only mnt_leave_cmd holds USAGE ON SCHEMA leave_api (0166), and it may already call create_employee, so there is no privilege gain and no reach from mnt_rt. What is real: a SECURITY DEFINER authorization predicate over users/role assignments is callable with an arbitrary p_org_id, and the deny-by-default tripwire built to catch exactly that is red on the spine.
fix: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION leave_api.assert_employee_directory_manager(UUID, UUID) FROM PUBLIC, mnt_rt, mnt_leave_cmd;
then: The privilege-matrix assertion must be widened to seven — adding only create_employee, the one deliberate new entrypoint. It must NOT be widened to include the helper: that would delete the invariant instead of restoring it.
